articles.title: 7 Funniest 'Far Side' Comics About Food
articles.summary: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic. While most of them featured stupid humans or talking animals as their main characters, the surrealist streak in cartoonist Gary Larson sometimes gave life to inanimate objects as well.
body: Here are the seven funniest Far Side comics that star food, some of which feature food that has even gained sentience for the sake of a perfect joke.

I love this comic strip because it is just unabashedly silly. Not only are sandwiches alive in this one-panel reality, but they have such a complex social structure that they even have their own organized crime. The sandwich mafia is so cruel that it punishes its victims by hurling them into a pit of fourth-graders. If I were the sandwich, I’d be especially worried about the fourth-grader in the green stripey shirt. He looks vicious.
Yet another food item that has turned to a life of crime. Here, Larson interprets potato salad going bad in the silliest way possible​​​​​​​.

This is a twist on that classic gag where, with two people in a life boat, one begins to imagine the other as food. This one features​​​​​​​ a man and a cow in a lifeboat​​​​​​​, so the man naturally imagines steak while looking at the cow​​​​​​​. As for the cow, well, he dreams of the man as a pile of man-shaped grass.
points: Anything can be the star of a Far Side comic.
While most of them featured stupid humans or talking animals as their main characters, the surrealist streak in cartoonist Gary Larson sometimes gave life to inanimate objects as well.

articles.title: 63 Years Later, CBS's Legendary 70-Episode Series Still Has the Only Vampire Worth Watching
articles.summary: It’s Fangsgiving here at Polygon, our Thanksgiving celebration of stories about fanged creatures of all types and especially vampires. I didn't want to be left out, but, to be honest, I always thought vampires were kind of dumb. They're a horror movie staple, but they’re rarely all that scary.
body: The only vampire character I ever really had any affection for is Grandpa Munster from the 1964 black-and-white sitcom The Munsters.

The Munsters debuted in 1964 and lasted for just two seasons, but in that time they produced a whopping 70 episodes. The show is about a family of monsters living a normal life in the suburbs and freaking out nearly everyone they encounter. The head of the family is Herman Munster (Fred Gwynne), who is Frankenstein’s monster. He is married to a vampire named Lily (Yvonne De Carlo), and they have​​​​​​​ a werewolf son named Eddie (Butch Patrick). Also living with them is their entirely normal, non-monster niece, Marilyn (Beverley Owen/Pat Priest). And best of all is Grandpa Munster, a several-hundred-year-old vampire​​​​​​​ played by Al Lewis.

To be clear, Grandpa is a pretty crappy vampire. A running gag on the show is his trying (and failing) to bite people. He also can go out during the day and casts a reflection without issue. So, really, he’s a vampire in name only, which might scare off some vampire purists. But if you’re interested in checking out some great Grandpa-centric episodes of The Munsters, here are five of the best.

articles.summary: Warframe 's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new update, which arrives on 9th December.
body: In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford said. "It is a second solar system... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a new solar system brick-by-brick."

That begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a new navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The World-Seeder Oasis is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

articles.title: After drawing ire for selling new Mass Effect merch following BioWare closure, EA is now flogging new Dragon Age tat too
articles.summary: Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.
body: EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, quickly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, new Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time ( thanks IGN ) to promote a new "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

articles.title: The better version of the wireless headset I love is $40 off right now
articles.summary: Inzone H9 Wireless Gaming Headset: was $178.99 now $138.99 This is the first generation of this headset, hence the better price. A lightweight, super comfortable, wireless, and reliable headset. Great audio for both gaming and media, and impressive built-in noise cancelling.
body: The Inzone H9 headset isn't a flashy or particularly popular headset, but it really should be in conversation among the best wireless options. This is a great pair of headphones on discount for Black Friday—a $40 cut at $138.

I had never heard Inzone when I picked up a pair of H6's (the lesser model to the H9) at Best Buy a year ago. It's a newish brand within Sony for gaming peripherals marketed toward both console and PC. I was just desperate for a headset that wouldn't fall apart and the price was right, so I gave them a shot. I was quickly impressed.

The audio quality was seriously good for the price, and they were also the most comfortable headset I've ever owned for two reasons: They're very light for a wireless headset and they don't squeeze my large head.

The H9 set above is better than the H6 in basically every way—better battery life (32 hours), noise cancelling, support for both 2.4 Ghz and Bluetooth connections—and during Black Friday it's only $20 more. So as much as I love my budget-friendly pair, there's little reason not to upgrade.

"Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post.

"We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

articles.title: The canonical USB microphone is still great, and now a total steal for $70
articles.summary: Blue Yeti USB Microphone: was $99.99 now $69.99 I've used a Blue Yeti for nearly a decade and it would happily serve for a decade more. A classic design, good hardware controls, and zero fuss.
body: The Blue Yeti might be the most popular USB microphone ever made, and you know what, it earned it. At its usual price, this is a great USB microphone. At $69.99 (its lowest price ever), it's simply one of the best bangs for your buck in this category.

The original Blue Yeti released in 2009, and in 17 years it has barely changed. I've had mine for a decade, and as I look around, I'm realizing it is the longest-lasting gadget on my desk. That's because it just works: I plug in, adjust the gain, and my voice comes through clear.

These days there are more advanced microphones than the Yeti, like its official sequel the Yeti 2, and certainly mics that are just as competitively priced. Those are good too, and I encourage you to check out cheaper options (like the $26 Amazon Basics mic that we surprisingly love ) before making any decisions.

body: From pioneers like Doom and Half-Life to multiplayer classics like Counter-Strike and Left 4 Dead 2, here are the 30 First-Person Shooter Masterpieces You Need to Play.
points: Part of the promise of video games is putting yourself in another world, taking control of a character and experiencing adventure and excitement through their eyes.
No genre takes this premise quite so literally as the first-person shooter, a pillar of the medium and a fundamental building block of…
There’s no shortage of great first-person shooters, but a select few stand above the rest as high-water marks for the art form.
From pioneers like Doom and Half-Life to multiplayer classics like Counter-Strike and Left 4 Dead 2, here are the 30 First-Person Shooter Masterpieces You Need to Play.

videos.title: Labyrinthine - Lost in the Sands Coming Out December 10 | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Venture into the scorching wastes of ancient Egypt in Lost in the Sands, a new DLC for Labyrinthine, a co-op survival horror game.
body: Explore shifting sand dunes, descend into an ancient Egyptian temple, and face new enemies.
Featuring two new maps with new puzzles, new cosmetics, lobby music, and an official crossover with FOREWARNED.
Coming to PlayStation on December 10!
